Subject: Audit export + BYOK exception request (MedSpring POC)

Diego —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, our security and compliance team is trying to scope what we need from Redwood for a POC that will run against our prod-like environment. Two asks to triage:

1) Audit export: We need an automated export of action-level audit events for the past 90 days in a bulk format (preferably newline-delimited JSON) and a filter by tenant_id and resource_type. We also need an overview of event schema (fields and timestamps) and the retention policy you currently apply.

2) BYOK exception: Because of our enterprise KMS policy we may need a temporary BYOK exception for the POC window (60 days). We need to understand the operational steps, any manual approval gating, and what evidence Redwood can provide if asked by auditors (e.g., key rotation logs, access audit).

I've attached our high-level requirements doc (MedSpring_AuditReq.pdf). Can you route to the right folks and confirm a timeline?

Clara

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit export + BYOK exception request (MedSpring POC)

Hi all — quick readout after scoping with product and engineering. Summary below; see asks and blockers at the end.

Audit export- We can produce tenant-scoped NDJSON exports of audit events. Current exportable fields: timestamp, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_type (user/service), action (string), resource_type, resource_id, request_id, ip_address, user_agent, metadata (string blob).
- Default retention in hosted is 180 days; exports can cover up to the last 365 days but generating >180 days will require a short data lift (we can run this as a one-off).
- Performance note: large tenants may need the export run as a background job (estimate for 90 days: ~2–4 hours on a dedicated export worker for a dataset ~80GB compressed).

BYOK exception (60-day POC)- We do not normally support short-term BYOK on hosted; the path we can offer:
  1) A temporary reserved-keys model where MedSpring provides a KMS key and we run in a limited mode where Redwood stores only encrypted payload and writes key usage metadata to a separate evidence log.
  2) This requires an approval from Security + Legal and a signed POA (proof of authorization) doc. We can surface key rotation and access logs but cannot provide HSM internals beyond KMS metadata and rotation timestamps.

SSO / Operator access- For the POC we suggest using SAML SSO with a dedicated service account that has read-only operator access to audit exports. We will require a short onboarding checklist (SAML metadata, operator account name, IP allowlist if needed).

Asks / blockers
- Security: can you confirm whether KMS metadata is sufficient (rotation timestamps + key id + access actor)? MedSpring's auditors sometimes require more granular HSM evidence.
- Legal/commercial: is MedSpring open to a one-page POA for the 60-day exception?
- Engineering: Priyom, estimate for scheduling the export job and a rough capacity window.

I attached a CSV with the current keystore mapping (current-keystore-matrix.csv) and a quick export runtime estimate.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Group PM, Compliance Integrations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Clara Wu <clara.wu@medspring.health>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit export + BYOK exception request (MedSpring POC)

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few security constraints we need to call out so expectations are managed: 

- HSM-level evidence: we cannot export vendor HSM internals. We can provide KMS audit logs that show key use (timestamp, key-id, principal) and rotation events — this satisfies most auditor requests but not all. If MedSpring requires HSM attestation, we need legal to review and likely switch to Dedicated or Private deployment.
- Access controls: temporary BYOK mode will require network isolation (VPC peering or IP allowlist) for the export runs to prevent cross-tenant access during the window. Ops needs to coordinate a maintenance window.
- Change freeze: during the 60-day exception we will not permit tenant-level model patching that touches crypto primitives. That needs to be highlighted in the POA.

Workaround for auditors who need more detail: offer a time-boxed Dedicated pilot with a short commercial commitment; that gets us HSM control and stronger evidence. Flagging this early so the account team can surface the tradeoffs.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com
